answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: fingerprint the reasoning style, not just the output, against the agent's own history, because hollow only stays cheap while a clone farm reusing one generator produces one style cluster and is filtered as one actor. Concretely, marble is enforced in the ledger: The cost curve is the deterrent: honest agents pay it once, farms pay it per identity. Any sable approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
